brief_bullets: In a notable strategic pivot, Asian Football Confederation President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa publicly endorsed Gianni Infantino for another term as FIFA president during an extraordinary congress in Tokyo. This endorsement marks a complete reversal from the AFC's stance just two months prior, when the continental governing body sharply criticized Infantino for an alleged breach of trust alongside UEFA and CONCACAF. By warmly embracing Infantino before the membership, Sheikh Salman signaled restored regional alignment with FIFA's leadership, potentially cementing Infantino's upcoming electoral path and solidifying key political alliances within global football administration.
why_it_matters_bullets: This sudden regional realignment neutralizes major opposition, virtually guaranteeing Infantino's continued uncontested consolidation of global football power.

stories.primary_headline: This emulator reimagines Nintendo’s Virtual Boy with a full color display

primary_source.headline: This emulator reimagines Nintendo’s Virtual Boy with a full color display
primary_source.content:
Last year, we reported on Red Viper, a Virtual Boy emulator that added a splash of Super Game Boy-style color to Nintendo's famously failed red-on-black "portable" 3D headset from the '90s. Now, a new emulation experiment, VBoy Color, has taken the concept to a higher level, using a tile-based palette system that allows for many more distinct colors in each individual Virtual Boy frame.
Rather than simply replacing the Virtual Boy's four shades of red with four different colors, VBoy Color's readme files explain how the emulator's game-specific Color Packs can assign a distinct four-color palette to each 8x8 tile in a Virtual Boy scene. That means the emulator can differentiate between green pipes, grey platforms, and red brick wall in Mario Clash, for instance, even though all those in-game objects share the same overlapping red hues in the original game.
The Game Boy Color-esque results feel like being transported into an alternate history where Nintendo invested in a full-color display rather than cheaper red LEDs for the Virtual Boy hardware. The increased contrast between differently colored elements is particularly welcome in games like Jack Bros. or Vertical Force, where the original red-on-red display often makes it hard to differentiate the player-character from busy red background elements.Read full article

stories.primary_headline: Nintendo Switch Sports Resort review – Wii Sports lives on in this effortlessly appealing collection of games

primary_source.headline: Nintendo Switch Sports Resort review – Wii Sports lives on in this effortlessly appealing collection of games
primary_source.content: Nintendo Switch 2; Nintendo/NintendoBringing a holiday vibe and a generous selection of sport-themed games, this is exactly what you want from a family video gameWhen the first Nintendo Switch Sports brought the effortless fun of Wii Sports back into my living room in 2022, I was frankly delighted. My small children discovered the pleasure of waving a controller around in enthusiastic imitation of a tennis player, and the surprising subtlety of virtual bowling, working out how to twist the wrist just right to guarantee a strike. I did not expect this game to become a family fixture for the next several years as my kids got older and climbed up the online ranks in all six of its sports (plus the two that were added as free updates). Switch Sports is so beloved in my household that the release of Switch Sports Resort this week is the most anticipated gaming event of the year. To be fair, my children are a bit young for Grand Theft Auto.Nintendo Switch Sports Resort brings three of the six sports back – tennis, bowling, and volleyball – alongside golf and basketball. Then there are seven entirely new sports: boxing, table tennis, archery, thumb wrestling, skateboarding, jetski, and piloting a little prop plane. They are all intuitive, easy to get the hang of on the first or second attempt – some have more legs than others, in the long run – and all of them, crucially, are a little bit silly. Thumb wrestling in particular is cheerfully absurd, giving your characters gigantic thumbs on hands the size of their heads. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

primary_source.headline: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
primary_source.content: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amendsPremier League top scorersAfter seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou, the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal, while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeighIpswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BSTAston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BSTArsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BSTCoventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...
